key_insight: Combining physics-based simulation and neural networks mapped HDPE friction stir welding quality, identifying 1500 rpm, 30 mm/min and 60 °C bottom preheating as optimal within the tested conditions.
engineering_relevance: Bottom preheating reduced peak plunge force from 1600 N to about 1100 N, supporting more stable welding and defect-resistant HDPE joints.
method: Developed a 3D Coupled Eulerian–Lagrangian model of temperature, force, material flow and defect formation.
Trained two multilayer perceptron neural networks on experimental temperature and axial-force data.
Combined simulation and ANN predictions to map defective and defect-free process windows.
evidence_signal: Experiments validated simulated thermal, mechanical and void-formation responses; ANN temperature and force predictions achieved R² values of 0.91–0.99 across tested conditions.
watch_item: Performance beyond the tested processing conditions remains unestablished, so new operating ranges require validation.
paper_title: Computational and machine learning modelling approaches for weld quality predictions in friction stir welding of high-density polyethylene
